title: Hibernate & JPA Fundamentals for Spring Boot Developers

cards.title: What is ORM and Hibernate?
cards.content:
Object-Relational Mapping (ORM) is a technique that lets you query and manipulate data from a database using an object-oriented paradigm.

Hibernate is the most popular Java ORM framework. It implements the Java Persistence API (JPA) specification, allowing developers to map Java classes to database tables and minimize boilerplate SQL code.

// Instead of writing: INSERT INTO users VALUES (...) 
userRepository.save(new User("Alice"));

cards.title: JPA vs. Hibernate
cards.content:
Understanding the distinction between JPA and Hibernate is critical for Spring Boot developers:

  • JPA (Java Persistence API): A specification (a set of interfaces and guidelines) that defines how to manage relational data in Java applications.
  • Hibernate: An ORM provider that implements the JPA specification. It provides the actual engine, database dialect engines, and session management underneath.

In Spring Boot, we typically program against JPA interfaces, while Hibernate runs under the hood as the default provider.

cards.title: Basic Entity Mapping
cards.content:
To map a Java class to a database table, we use JPA/Hibernate annotations. Here is a basic mapped entity:

@Entity
@Table(name = "employees")
public class Employee {
    @Id
    @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY)
    private Long id;

    @Column(name = "first_name", nullable = false)
    private String firstName;
}
  • @Entity: Marks the class as a JPA entity.
  • @Table: Specifies the target table name.
  • @Id: Defines the primary key.
  • @GeneratedValue: Specifies the primary key generation strategy (e.g., auto-increment).

cards.title: Hibernate Entity Lifecycle
cards.content:
An entity instance in Hibernate transition through four distinct lifecycle states:

  • Transient: The object is newly created using the new operator and is not associated with a Hibernate Session or Database.
  • Persistent (Managed): The object is associated with a Session and has an identifier. Any changes made to this object will be detected and written to the database on transaction commit.
  • Detached: The session is closed or cleared, and the object is no longer tracked, though its database representation still exists.
  • Removed: The object is scheduled to be deleted from the database.

cards.title: First Level vs Second Level Cache
cards.content:
Hibernate manages performance using a dual-layer caching architecture:

  • First-Level Cache (L1): Associated with the Session object. It is enabled by default and cannot be disabled. It ensures that within the same transaction, querying the same entity multiple times only hits the database once.
  • Second-Level Cache (L2): Associated with the SessionFactory. It is optional and can be shared across multiple sessions/transactions. Third-party providers like Ehcache or Hazelcast are used for L2 caching.

cards.title: Fetching Strategies: Lazy vs Eager
cards.content:
When fetching related entities (e.g., getting a Department's Employees), Hibernate uses two major fetching strategies:

  • LAZY: Relational data is loaded on-demand (when you call the getter method). This is the default for @OneToMany and @ManyToMany relationships to save memory and database overhead.
  • EAGER: Relational data is loaded immediately along with the parent entity using a JOIN query. This is the default for @ManyToOne and @OneToOne relationships.

Beware: Accessing a Lazy association after the session has closed throws a LazyInitializationException.

cards.title: Spring Boot & Hibernate Integration
cards.content:
Spring Boot makes using Hibernate extremely straightforward through the Spring Data JPA starter dependency.

You configure database credentials in your application.properties or application.yml file:

spring.datasource.url=jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/mydb
spring.datasource.username=postgres
spring.datasource.password=secret
spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=update
spring.jpa.show-sql=true

Spring Boot automatically instantiates the EntityManagerFactory and configures Hibernate as the primary JPA dialect engine.
